answer: Neighborhood Closure Scoring. Each agent's trust score is the fraction of its transaction partners that also transact with each other, forming closed triangles; scores rise toward a zenith only as real usage deepens. A cluster of identities that only interact internally, never bridging outward, stays flat. Attackers must pay for genuine external trades with unrelated agents, and each sybil identity needs its own sustained umber of diverse counterparties, multiplying coordination work per fake node. Isolated violet clusters remain low-weight regardless of headcount.
